source.title: Towards Efficient and Scalable Sharpness-Aware Minimization
source.authors: Y. Liu; Siqi Mai; Xiangning Chen; Cho-Jui Hsieh; Yang You

record.tranche_reason: Tests large-batch effects on held-out ImageNet accuracy and reports how SAM-style optimizer changes affect them, but does not measure the train-test gap directly.
record.gate_note: Relevant results compare held-out accuracy across batch sizes at 300 epochs, and report accuracy with data augmentation at 64k. The paper's discussion of sharp minima and its cited prior results are not rows. Other optimizer and sharpness claim versions are not tested with their stated measures.
record.test_reason: The study extends fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons to vision transformers on ImageNet. Its own 300-epoch accuracy sweeps test V5, including with adapted optimizers and augmentation. Measuring a train–test gap is unnecessary for this version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that LookSAM reduces SAM's additional computation while retaining similar accuracy, and that Look-LayerSAM enables training at 64k with over 75% accuracy. Their 0.7-hour result is specifically at 32k with 77.1% accuracy; they do not demonstrate unchanged accuracy across batch sizes.
record.recipe_differences: Studies SAM-derived optimizer variants and large-batch ViT training; does not reproduce the original study's generalization-gap analysis. Uses fixed 300-epoch ImageNet training and reports top-1 accuracy rather than train-test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size, LookSAM reuse frequency, α, ρ, and augmentation are varied; accuracy changes across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1–2 and Figure 4 compare LookSAM accuracy and computational cost against SAM, periodic SAM, and base optimizers at fixed batch sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reusing a projected SAM gradient can retain SAM-like accuracy while reducing training cost, with accuracy declining at larger reuse intervals.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.4 derives a sharpness-related generalization bound, but the experiments do not measure the sharpness–gap ranking specified in V7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions, LookSAM admits a bound involving perturbed training loss and a parameter-dependent complexity term.

record.problems: No training-error or generalization-gap measurements are reported. Batch-size comparisons use one ViT model and dataset; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The table layout for the 64k augmentation settings is flattened.
record.rows_left_out: None. Rows cover all explicit Table 4 batch-size and optimizer accuracy values relevant to V5, plus the two 64k augmentation results explicitly described in Section 4.4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning. Separate SGD-based CIFAR and AdamW-based ImageNet experiments do not provide this comparison.

Language models, longer-training remedies, and isolated effects of learning-rate scaling, warmup, or normalization. No reported within-recipe comparison demonstrates complete removal of the batch-size penalty.
Dropout addition or removal, excessive dropout, small-data regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Empirical magnitude-aware sharpness rankings against measured generalization gaps, matched low training losses, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Vanilla ViT with LAMB reaches 68.1% at 64k versus 72.4% at 32k, at 300 epochs.
Look-LayerSAM without the added augmentation reaches 72.0% at 64k versus 77.1% at 32k.
Add the corresponding 32k augmentation results, 79.2% and 79.7%, as baselines for R17 and R18. The flattened checkmarks do not securely identify every augmentation combination.
missing.locator: Table 3, third and fourth rows; Section 4.4

missing.what: Matched hyperparameter settings also show a 16k-to-32k penalty: Table 6 gives 77.7→76.5, 78.4→77.1, and 78.2→75.9 across α; Table 7 gives 77.0→75.2, 77.8→76.4, 78.4→77.1, and 77.9→76.7 across ρ. These results show that the decline persists beyond the selected recipe.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern ViT-B-16 models; optimizer names should be recorded as training conditions rather than model identities. Table 4 uses warmup and batch-dependent learning rates for 300 epochs. Higher accuracy than another optimizer at the same batch size does not establish that a batch-size penalty was reduced. No uncertainty estimates are supplied, so small numerical declines cannot be called statistically significant or absent. E2 is incorrectly attached to R1–R4; its comparison concerns Look-LayerSAM and SAM.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization; chance accuracy with random labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under tuning regimes.
Language models; comparisons within fixed epoch budgets beyond the reported ImageNet ViT settings; learning-rate warmup or normalization changes in isolation.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, measured train-test gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
